requirements.title: License number displayed in website advertising
requirements.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code 7030.5

criteria: Website advertises construction/electrical contracting services in California (pacificplainselectric.com).
Also applies to Volteira-hosted contractor pages/booking pages that advertise a tenant's services.

required_behavior: The contractor's CSLB license number appears in all forms of advertising, including the website.

How to check: (1) the license number (digits, typically labelled 'CSLB Lic. #' or 'CA Lic. #') is visible on the homepage and in the footer of every page template, and on paid/landing pages and booking pages; (2) the number is real text (not only in an image) so it can be read and searched; (3) the same number appears on linked profiles the site controls (Google Business Profile, Yelp, social pages) as a best practice; (4) the number matches the CSLB record for the advertised business name (see WEB-CSLB-002).
requirements.enforcement_exposure: Citation and civil penalty by CSLB; failure is a cause for disciplinary action.
required_evidence: screenshot of license number on homepage and footer

requirements.title: License active and advertised business name matches CSLB record
requirements.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code 7059.1; 7028 (unlicensed contracting); 7027.1

criteria: Website advertises construction/electrical contracting services in California (pacificplainselectric.com).
Also applies to Volteira-hosted contractor pages/booking pages that advertise a tenant's services.

required_behavior: The license shown is current and active on the CSLB public license lookup on the audit date (not expired, suspended or inactive).
The business name used on the site (and in ads) is the name on the CSLB license record (or an approved DBA on the record); the site does not advertise under a different or misleading name.

requirements.title: Online home improvement contract contains statutory contents
requirements.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code 7159(c)-(e)
requirements.amendment_notes: AB 1327 (Stats. 2025) added contractor email/telephone and email Notice of Cancellation provisions (per secondary sources and CSLB 2026 new-laws bulletin); not verified against official text.

criteria: A home improvement contract (work on residential property, aggregate contract price over the statutory threshold, $500 under B&P 7159 per prior knowledge — confirm current threshold) is formed, signed or accepted online (e-signature, click-to-accept estimate, or online deposit that accepts an estimate).
business_types: pacificplainselectric.com and any Volteira-hosted estimate/contract acceptance page used by Pacific Plains Electric
exceptions: Service and repair contracts meeting B&P 7159.10 et seq. have separate, alternative requirements (see WEB-CSLB-016).
Commercial (non-residential) work is outside 7159.

required_behavior: The e-signed or click-accepted contract includes the 7159 contents as required, including: heading 'Home Improvement' (contract), contractor name, business address, license number; the CSLB information notice; salesperson name/registration if applicable; contract price and finance charges; description of work and materials; approximate start and substantial completion dates; schedule of progress payments; the down payment statement; the Mechanics Lien Warning; the right-to-cancel notice when applicable; required statements about change orders, commercial general liability and workers' compensation insurance; and the contractor's email address and statement that the Notice of Cancellation may be emailed (AB 1327).
Contract is presented in full to the buyer before signature (not only a summary).
requirements.enforcement_exposure: Noncompliant contracts: CSLB discipline, misdemeanor exposure under 7159, and potential unenforceability/restitution claims.
required_evidence: copy of the online contract template

requirements.title: Right-to-cancel notice for home solicitation / online-formed contracts (applicability)
requirements.citation: Cal. Civ. Code 1689.5-1689.7 (home solicitation contracts), 1689.6 (home repair/emergency), 7159(e) notice; senior buyers 65+ five-day period

exceptions: Service and repair contracts meeting B&P 7159.10 et seq. have separate, alternative requirements (see WEB-CSLB-016).
Commercial (non-residential) work is outside 7159.

required_behavior: Determine whether contracts formed online (or negotiated in the buyer's home and signed online) are 'home solicitation contracts' (made at a place other than the seller's appropriate trade premises) requiring the three-business-day (five business days for buyers 65 or older) right to cancel and the statutory Notice of Cancellation form.

Where applicable, the e-sign flow presents the Notice of Cancellation in the required form and size, with the contractor's address and email for cancellation, and the contractor does not begin work or take payment in violation of the cancellation period (except qualifying emergency repairs with the buyer's waiver).

criteria: Site books California diagnostic visits online

required_behavior: Public pages and booking flows show the diagnostic fee, $0.00 due today and the amount due upon completion; never describe the fee as a deposit or as paid at booking.
